title: A Microphysiological System to Study Leukocyte-Endothelial Cell Interaction during Inflammation
protocol: Insert tubing into all ports except one inlet port on the bMFA device.
Load a syringe with prepared fibronectin solution.
Connect the syringe to a blunt needle and long tubing.
Push the plunger until fibronectin comes out of the other inlet port, then clamp it.
Repeat this process for the rest of the ports until all channels, tissue compartment, and tubing are filled with human fibronectin solution.
Fill tubing with fibronectin before clamping.
Connect unclamped tubing to Pneumatic Primer, adjust pressure to ~5 psi and run for ~15 min.
Check under microscope to ensure no air bubbles are trapped in the device.
Reconnect device to Pneumatic Primer if air bubbles are present and repeat degassing process.
Incubate device at 37 °C for 1 h after removing from Pneumatic Primer.
Flush all channels and tissue compartment with pre-warmed HLMVEC culture media.
Seed bMFA with HLMVEC cultured to 60%-80% confluency in a T-25 flask.
Aspirate HLMVEC culture media from cell culture flask.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
Add 2 ml of pre-warmed trypsin-EDTA solution in the T-25 flask.
Incubate for 3-5 min until most cells are detached from the flask.
Add 2 mL of Trypsin Neutralization Solution (TNS) at 37 °C to the flask.
Gently tap the flask to help dissociate the cells.
Transfer the cell suspension solution to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 150 x g to pellet the endothelial cells.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cells in 3 mL of cell culture media.
Count the number of cells with a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge again for 5 min at 150 x g to pellet the cells.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cells to a seeding density of 20 x 10^6/mL.
Mount a 1 mL syringe in the programmable syringe pump, attach tubing to the blunt needle.
Draw ~20 µL of the cell suspension into the tubing, ensuring no cell suspension is in the syringe barrel.
Take the clamp off an outlet port of the device.
Connect the tubing to one inlet of the device, ensuring no air bubbles are introduced.
Start the pump with a flow rate of 4-8 µL/min.
Observe the device under a microscope for channel filling.
When channels are filled with cells, stop the pump and clamp the outlet.
Cut the inlet tubing.
Put the device in the incubator for 4 h at 5% CO2 and 37 °C.
Prepare another syringe filled with fresh cell culture media after 4 h.
Mount the syringe on a syringe pump and connect it to an inlet port.
Connect the syringe to an outlet port and remove the clamp from it.
Run fresh media through the device for about 5 min at 4-8 µL/min.
Prepare a syringe filled with fresh cell culture media for culturing endothelial cells under flow.
Mount the syringe in a syringe pump and connect it to one inlet port.
Keep an outlet open for culturing endothelial cells under flow.
Put the device in the incubator (5% CO2, 37 °C) for culturing endothelial cells under flow.
Check bMFA under a microscope after 48 h of culture under flow.
Prepare three different bMFA devices using the protocol mentioned above.
Load one syringe with cell culture media for treatment.
Load another syringe with TNF-α (10 ng/mL) for treatment.
Load another syringe with TNF-α (10 ng/mL) + PKCδ-i (5 µM) for treatment.
Connect three syringes to three bMFA devices.
Treat HLMVEC with buffer TNF-α or TNF-α + inhibitor for 4 h at 0.1 µL/min.
Pipette 20 mL of leukocyte isolation media into a 50 mL conical tube.
Carefully layer 25 mL of blood over the leukocyte isolation media.
Centrifuge for 40 min at 427 x g at room temperature.
Aspirate down to ~5 mL above red blood cells (RBC) layer.
Add HEPES buffer to double the current volume.
Calculate and add an amount of 6% Dextran, which will be 20% of the final volume.
Invert the tube gently a few times to mix well.
Let the RBC sediment (~25 min).
Carefully pipette the upper layer (neutrophil-rich layer) and transfer to a new 50 mL tube.
Be careful not to contaminate with sedimented RBC.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 315 x g at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 8 mL of HEPES buffer.
Add 24 mL of DI water to lyse residual RBCs, mix gently for 50 s.
Immediately add 8 mL of 3.6% NaCl solution, mix well.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 315 x g at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant and wash the cell pellet with 15 mL of HEPES buffer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 315 x g.
Resuspend the pellet in HEPES buffer.
Resuspend isolated human neutrophils (15 million) in 999 µL of HEPES buffer.
Add 1 µL CFDA-SE dye stock solution (10 mM) to neutrophil suspension to obtain a working concentration of 10 µM CFDA-SE.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash the cells twice with HEPES buffer by centrifuging for 5 min at 315 x g.
Count the neutrophils using a hemocytometer and resuspend at 2 million neutrophils/mL in cell culture media, TNF-α (10 ng/mL), or TNF-α (10 ng/mL) + PKCδ-i (5 μM).
Incubate for 15 min at room temperature before the start of the experiment.
Prepare a syringe filled with 1 µM N-formyl-met-leu-phe (fMLP) in cell culture media.
Remove the tissue compartment port tubing and insert the fMLP tubing.
Inject ~20 µL of fMLP into the tissue compartment for all bMFA except the one treated with cell culture media alone.
Cut the tubing and clamp it.
Fill the syringe with ~200 µL of the neutrophil suspension.
Mount the syringe on the syringe pump.
Put the device on the inverted microscope stage (Table of Materials).
Start the pump at a flow rate of 1 µL/min.
Wait until a small drop of the neutrophil suspension comes out of the tubing.
Insert the tubing into the inlet port.
Acquire images using the Scan Large Image function in the microscope image analysis software to obtain the adhesion map in bMFA 10 min after starting the experiment.
Take timelapse images every 5 minutes during the next hour for migration analysis.
Count the number of adhered neutrophils in each vessel for the adhesion map.
Create a circular region of interest (ROI) with a diameter equal to two times the vessel diameter at each bifurcation.
Count the number of adhered neutrophils within the ROI using manual count or automated Object Count function.
Determine the shear rate in each vessel using the shear rate map generated from CFD simulation.
Plot the number of adhered neutrophils against the shear rate for each vessel to create a shear rate map.
Count the number of neutrophils that have crossed through the endothelium into the tissue compartment as migrated neutrophils.
Count the number of migrated neutrophils at 10 min, 15 min, 30 min and 60 min.
Plot the number of migrated neutrophils versus time.
